data.gender_notes: Bhupal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit 'Bhu' meaning 'Earth' and 'Pal' meaning 'Lord'. Bhupal is a name for one who rules or governs the earth. In Hindu mythology, Bhupal is a title given to various deities and rulers. It is also a common name among Hindu communities. The name Bhupal carries the meaning “Lord of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhupal usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Its usage can be traced back to the ancient Indian texts, where gods and heroes bearing this name are portrayed as powerful and just rulers.

historical_references.reference: Bhupal was a Jat ruler of the Chauhan dynasty in Rajasthan. He is known to have ruled between 1150 AD and 1185 AD.
Bhupal was a Rajput warrior who is said to have led the defense of Chittorgarh against the Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khilji in 1303 AD. He was killed during the siege.
